event.name: UFC 334: Gane vs. Hokit
event.notes: "mode": "auto" means every run resolves this itself — before config.json is even loaded, it asks ESPN for the soonest upcoming card, and if that differs from "name" below it rewrites "name"/"league"/"date", regenerates discovery.title_contains and discovery.search.queries from the new main event's fighters, and clears tracker.picks_videos (a stale roundup URL would just burn a download and a vision pass on the old event's deck). Once this week's card has happened, the next run rolls to whatever's next on its own — no manual retarget. "name"/"league"/"date" below are simply the last-resolved event; edit them by hand only if you delete "mode" and want to pin a specific card again (e.g. a Contender Series week, matched as a substring against ESPN's own event name — punctuation and case ignored, spelling not). "league" pins which scoreboard is searched (ufc / pfl); leave it empty to try UFC then PFL. Add more cards to the top-level "events" array to cover them in the same run — a PFL event the same weekend, say — and the dashboard puts a card selector at the top. If a run logs "No ESPN card found" (or, in auto mode, "No upcoming event found"), something's off with the league or the scoreboard is unreachable — nothing is filtered and off-card fights come back.

notes: Welterweight. The field, the panels and the oddsmakers all have Medic by KO at +108, but the best method predictors go the other way — 2 of 3 on a Holland submission.
Welterweight prelim headliner, and Thompson's retirement fight. Not one channel picked a submission.
FLAG — the host gave this method split without stating its total, so the usual reconciliation check could not run; 58 is the sum of the counts he read out.
He also said the best method predictors were split between Thompson's KO and his decision but gave no panel size, so no method-panel count is recorded.
Women's bantamweight title, co-main — Nunes's comeback after three years out.

The widest odds-versus-sharps gap on the card and the host's third best bet: Nunes is a +150 underdog, the field is a near coin flip at 54%, but 6 of 7 best predictors and 7 of 8 best favorite-pickers are on her. Only one of the eight best favorite-pickers has the champion.
The host said the method panel split between a Nunes KO and a Nunes decision but gave no panel size, so no method-panel count is recorded.
Lightweight. The field and the panels favour Duncan on the moneyline, but the single most-picked method is Dober by KO at +195 — and the best method predictors are there too.
Heavyweight title, main event. Hokit is 10-0 and unbeaten in four UFC fights inside eight months.
84% of the method votes have this ending inside the distance; Gane by KO pays +145 against his -190 moneyline.
The host said most best method predictors had Gane by KO but gave no panel size, so no method-panel count is recorded.
Middleweight. Borralho is the favourite in odds and nowhere else: the field, the best predictors, the best favorite-pickers and the best underdog-pickers all lean Belgaroui.
Middleweight. Every best method predictor has this ending by KO — they only disagree on who, and so do the oddsmakers.
Lightweight. Every panel is unanimous on Costa and 85 of 86 channels agree.
The host said the best method predictors split one for the KO and one for a decision but never gave the panel's size, so no method-panel count is recorded.
Lightweight; Miller's 48th UFC fight.
The most one-sided method read on the card: not one of the 59 channels has this going to the scorecards. Every channel on McKinney has the KO, every channel on Miller has the submission.
The host's second best bet: all three panels are 100% on McKinney, and his KO pays +140 against a -200 moneyline.
Women's bantamweight. Mesquita has won all three UFC fights by submission, and 89% of the method votes have her doing it again at -116.

Flyweight; opens the main card. The biggest favourite and the biggest underdog on the card, and the most lopsided fight the engine has recorded: all 84 channels and every panel on Hasan, and 64 of 65 method votes his KO.
The host read that KO share as 89.5%; the two counts he gave make it 98.5%. The counts are used.
He said every best method predictor had the KO but gave no panel size, so no method-panel count is recorded.
Lightweight, and the closest fight on the card in odds. The host's first best bet: Elder is the +100 underdog but takes 68% of the field and every sharp panel, and his decision pays +250.
Bantamweight; Heili replaced Adrian Yanez, who withdrew injured.
Unanimous on the winner — all 80 channels and every panel on Diaz — but the method vote is the most evenly spread on the card: 25 decision, 18 submission, 11 KO.
No method prices are posted yet; the bout was made late.
